dimensions.note: No secrets. The lock's claim is a random UUID that only matches a lock to the turn that made it; it is not a secret.
app_stand_in logs a claimed turn or that one is already running; app_stand_in_done logs who freed the request or that the turn no longer holds it.

Round 1 found release failing with No such key: next whenever the step failed; release now also depends on next succeeding, so it is skipped then (checked under serve). Round 1 also found release could fail on the login check and leave the request held; it now goes by the claim alone.

78 tests pass. They cover a held request refusing a second turn, a wrong token freeing nothing, the right one freeing it, a claim lapsing after 30 minutes, and a late release not freeing the turn that took over; a test checks release's dependencies. Mutating lockHeld to never hold fails the test. Under swamp serve with a 20s fake agent: two replies a second apart started one turn; a later reply took one; a turn with a missing agent failed and still freed the request; a failed step skipped release.

Swamp holds the behavior's lock for each workflow step under serve, and commits before releasing it, so two runs can't both find the request free. A turn longer than 30 minutes could outlast its claim, as swamp doesn't stop runs; the README recommends serve's --max-run-duration of 30 minutes or less.
The workflow takes no lock input; the token passes only from next's outputs to release. standInNext.lock defaults to empty.
One small lock record per request, freed by its turn; one left by a run that never finished lapses after 30 minutes.

Round 1 found the README overstated the guarantee; it now says the lock covers only turns the app brings in, not Slack's or hand-run ones, that an unfinished run holds it until it lapses, and to bound turns with --max-run-duration.
standInLock is fully typed; app_stand_in_done's id and lock are bounded strings.
standInLock is kept 1d with GC 2: one claim and one free per turn; an expired record reads as free.
Claimed by app_stand_in, freed by app_stand_in_done, lapsing on its own; no force-free is needed beyond the lapse.

The claim is made only once a turn is due (signed in, readable, open, one person, agent and stand-in set), and only if no held claim younger than 30 minutes exists. Round 1 found a failure between claim and decision could hold the request; the claim is now written last.
Reads and writes only its own behavior's lock record inside the locked step.
Manifest and all three behavior types at 2026.11.27.3 with identity upgrades; no settings changed.
